security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, code fences, placeholder URLs, and relative links. Confirmed risks are the intended use of external RunComfy CLI commands and third-party processing of prompts and image URLs.

remediation.issue: External API processing of user prompts and images
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear consent warning before sending confidential images, prompts, or private asset URLs to RunComfy.

remediation.issue: Shell command examples include user-controlled prompt content
remediation.suggestion: Recommend passing input through a file or structured argument builder to avoid shell quoting mistakes.

remediation.issue: Global CLI installation and token storage are prerequisites
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify the CLI package source and prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in automation environments.

content.user_title: Edit Images with GPT Image Edit on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Precise image edits can drift when prompts miss preservation, layout, or text details. This skill gives tested RunComfy GPT Image Edit patterns for controlled edits.
actual_capabilities: Builds RunComfy CLI requests for the openai/gpt-image-2/edit endpoint.
Guides preservation prompts for faces, products, brands, layout, and framing.
Supports up to 10 public HTTPS image references in the model input.
Provides patterns for multilingual in-image text replacement.
Explains supported size values and when to keep size set to auto.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and model API access.
Sends prompts and image URLs to RunComfy model infrastructure.
Does not provide batch editing beyond the model endpoint limits.
Cannot guarantee perfect text, identity, or layout preservation on every edit.

use_cases.title: Localize Campaign Images
use_cases.description: Replace in-image headlines with translated text while preserving the original layout and brand marks.

use_cases.title: Create Controlled Product Variants
use_cases.description: Change backgrounds, callouts, or layouts while keeping the product identity and framing stable.

use_cases.title: Compose Multi-Reference Scenes
use_cases.description: Combine a subject, room, and lighting reference with clear numbering in the edit prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Edit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner edit for one source image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Keep the main subject, pose, and framing unchanged. Replace the background with a clean studio setting.

prompt_templates.title: Localized Text Replacement
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate edit for ads, posters, or product labels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Keep the photo, logo, colors, and layout unchanged. Replace only the headline with the exact translated text I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Layout-Specific Revision
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced edit with precise placement instructions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Keep the image content unchanged except the callout. Move the callout to the lower right and preserve its style.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Reference Composition
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced edit using several image references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subject identity from image 1, room setting from image 2, and lighting style from image 3. Match them naturally.

output_examples.input: A campaign poster needs a Japanese headline while keeping the same product, logo, and layout.
output_examples.output: The skill produces preservation-first edit guidance with exact text quoting and script naming.

output_examples.input: A product photo needs a new studio background without changing the product shape or angle.
output_examples.output: The skill guides a focused background edit and recommends keeping size set to auto.

output_examples.input: A subject from one image should appear in a room from another image with matching light.
output_examples.output: The skill structures a numbered multi-reference prompt that separates identity, scene, and lighting cues.

best_practices: Start every edit prompt with the elements that must stay unchanged.
Use public HTTPS image URLs only after checking rights and privacy requirements.
Split complex creative changes into separate passes to reduce drift.
anti_patterns: Do not paste confidential images unless external processing is approved.
Do not combine many unrelated edits in one prompt.
Do not ask for unsupported size values.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images from text only?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the GPT Image 2 edit endpoint for image-to-image changes.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and access to the model API.

faq.question: Can it edit text inside images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill gives prompt patterns for exact multilingual text replacement.

faq.question: How many reference images can it use?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint accepts up to 10 public HTTPS image references.

faq.question: Does it keep images private on the local machine?
faq.answer: No. Prompts and image URLs are sent to RunComfy model infrastructure for processing.

faq.question: When should another model be used?
faq.answer: Use another model for large batch consistency, source-first local edits, or pure text-to-image generation.
